newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Feb industry employment down 0.4 pct vs Jan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Feb industry employment down 0.4 pct vs Jan.

text.p: Employment levels in Brazil's industrial sector fell 0.4 percent in February from January and 5.9 percent from February 1996, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
On a cumulative basis, the drop has been 6.2 percent so far this calendar year and 10.2 percent in the last 12 months.

Most of the sectors surveyed fired more people than they hired between January and February, with the exception of the tobacco industry, which employed 43.3 percent more workers, and to a much lesser extent the transport, pharmaceutical, plastic goods and chemical sectors.

Compared with employment levels in February 1996, the biggest losses were seen in the clothing sector (down 13.4 percent), the rubber industry (down 13.0 percent) and the mechanical sector (down 11.2 percent).
Total salaries paid in February fell 1.1 percent from January and were down 5.8 percent from February 1996.
